value: The Attorney-General is not a whole-time counsel for the Government
reasoning: Article 88 gives the Attorney-General the right to speak in both Houses, Article 76(3) gives a right of audience in all courts in India, and Article 76(1) requires the qualifications of a Supreme Court judge. He is not a full-time government counsel and may take private practice where it does not conflict with government work, so D is the incorrect statement.

value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; short notice questions are not taken during Question Hour
reasoning: A short notice question concerns a matter of urgent public importance, may be asked for oral answer at less than ten days' notice, and is admitted only if the Minister agrees to answer it at short notice. In the Lok Sabha it is taken up immediately after Question Hour, not during it, so statement 3 is wrong. Runner-up: A (all three), which would win only if 'after Question Hour' were read as part of the Question Hour sitting.

value: The Tenth Schedule does not make the Supreme Court the final arbiter of unresolved cases
reasoning: The Tenth Schedule provides disqualification for defection, exempts a valid merger (two-thirds of the legislature party), and leaves the decision to the Speaker or Chairman. It contains no provision making the Supreme Court a final arbiter; its paragraph 7 actually barred courts, and judicial review came later through the Kihoto Hollohan judgment (1992). Runner-up: B, which would be the answer only if the merger exception were read as unconditional.

value: All three pairs are correctly matched
reasoning: Public health and sanitation is Entry 6 of the State List, citizenship, naturalisation and aliens is Entry 17 of the Union List, and legal, medical and other professions is Entry 26 of the Concurrent List. All three pairs are correct.

value: Bacteria contain cytoplasm but viruses do not
reasoning: A bacterium is a cell with a membrane and cytoplasm, while a virus is only nucleic acid inside a protein coat with no cytoplasm. Neither has mitochondria (bacteria are prokaryotes), and viruses have no cell membrane, so B, C and D are false.

value: The cell loses water (exosmosis in a hypertonic medium)
reasoning: A surrounding medium more concentrated than the cell is hypertonic, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis and the cell shrinks (plasmolysis in plant cells).
Rough ER is studded with ribosomes on its outer surface, which give it the rough look under the microscope and let it make proteins. Smooth ER lacks them.

Apical meristem at the tips of stems and roots adds to their length. Lateral meristem increases girth, intercalary meristem lengthens internodes at their base, and secondary growth is growth in thickness.
The large central vacuole filled with cell sap presses the cytoplasm against the cell wall, and this turgor pressure keeps plant cells turgid and rigid.
Pollen grains are formed in the pollen sacs of the anther, the top part of the stamen. Stigma and style belong to the pistil and the corolla is the petals.

value: The marginal product of the variable factor will diminish
reasoning: The law of diminishing returns is a statement about physical output: adding more of a variable input to a fixed input eventually makes each extra unit add less output, so marginal product falls. It says nothing directly about revenue.

value: A monopolist's MR curve lies below, not above, its AR curve
reasoning: A monopolist faces a downward sloping demand (AR) curve, so to sell one more unit it must cut the price on all units and MR lies below AR. The other statements are true: a competitive firm's AR = MR is horizontal, it earns normal profit in the long run, and monopoly equilibrium (MR = MC) can occur with MC rising, falling or constant.

value: Quantity demanded does not change at all whatever the change in price
reasoning: Zero (perfectly inelastic) price elasticity means the demand curve is vertical: the quantity demanded stays the same however much the price changes.

Using average values: change in quantity is 80 on an average of 200, which is 40%, and change in price is 20 on an average of 100, which is 20%. Elasticity = 40/20 = 2.0. (The base-point method gives 1.5, which is not an option.)
The real interest rate is approximately the nominal rate minus inflation (Fisher relation): 24% - 10% = 14%.
Methanol is called wood spirit (wood alcohol) because it was first obtained by the destructive distillation of wood.

value: Lime juice (a true solution) will not show the Tyndall effect
reasoning: The Tyndall effect is scattering of light by particles large enough to see as a beam path: colloids such as starch solution and dilute milk, and suspensions such as chalk in water, all scatter light. Lime juice is treated as a true solution, whose particles are too small to scatter light. Runner-up: A, if the setter held that only colloids, not suspensions, show the effect.

Raising the pressure brings gas molecules closer together and lowering the temperature reduces their kinetic energy, both helping intermolecular attraction turn the gas into a liquid (below its critical temperature).
Bauxite is the ore of aluminium, magnetite (Fe3O4) of iron, malachite (a basic copper carbonate) of copper, and calamine (ZnCO3) of zinc, in the order given in A.
Citric acid has three carboxyl groups, tartaric acid two and lactic acid one. Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is a lactone whose acidity comes from an enol -OH group, not a carboxyl group.

value: Sulphuric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate solution
reasoning: In a soda-acid extinguisher, dilute sulphuric acid mixes with sodium hydrogencarbonate solution when the extinguisher is used, releasing carbon dioxide that pushes the liquid out onto the fire.

value: Surya Sen was not part of the Kakori case
reasoning: The Kakori train action (1925) was carried out by the Hindustan Republican Association; Ramprasad Bismil, Rajendra Lahiri and Ashfaqulla Khan were hanged in the case. Surya Sen led the Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930) in Bengal.

Bhagat Singh was influenced by socialist ideas and was a leading member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, so 1 and 2 are true. The 1929 Assembly bombs were deliberately thrown away from people to 'make the deaf hear', not to kill, so 3 is false.

His writings shaped modern Bengali prose (1 true) and he championed women's education (3 true). He received the title 'Vidyasagar' from Sanskrit College, Calcutta, not Presidency College (2 false), and he argued for widow remarriage on the basis of scripture, citing the Parashara Samhita (4 false).
On 13 April 1919 troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd in the enclosed Jallianwala Bagh at Amritsar without giving any warning to disperse. All three statements are true.
VVPAT was first used in the by-election to the Noksen Assembly constituency in Tuensang district, Nagaland, in September 2013. North Paravur, Kerala, is where EVMs were first used in 1982.

value: Unfinished business: the pursuit of rights and choices for all
reasoning: The UNFPA State of World Population 2019 report was titled 'Unfinished business: the pursuit of rights and choices for all'. 'Worlds apart' was the 2017 theme, 'The power of choice' the 2018 theme and the 'girl at this decisive age' report was 2016.

The Saraswati Samman for 2018 went to Telugu poet K Siva Reddy for his collection 'Pakkaki Ottigilite'. Mahabaleshwar Sail (2016), Padma Sachdev (2015) and Sitanshu Yashaschandra (2017) were earlier winners.
Kandhamal Haldi is grown by tribal farmers in Kandhamal district of southern Odisha and received a GI tag in 2019.
The Order of Zayed (Zayed Medal), named after Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, is the UAE's highest civilian honour; it was conferred on Prime Minister Modi in 2019.

In any mechanical wave, longitudinal included, the particles of the medium only oscillate about their mean positions; the disturbance and its energy travel through the medium, but the material itself is not carried along.
Uranium has atomic number 92, so U-235 has 92 protons and 235 - 92 = 143 neutrons.
Power P = F x v, so F = P / v = 3000 / 5 = 600 N.

value: An electromagnetic wave is transverse, not longitudinal
reasoning: In an electromagnetic wave the electric and magnetic fields oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, so the wave is transverse; that is also why it can be polarised. It carries energy and momentum and can be reflected, so A, B and D are true.
Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that needs a material medium. Light, radio waves and microwaves are all parts of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Diamond has a high refractive index (about 2.42) and so a small critical angle (about 24 degrees). Light entering a cut diamond is totally internally reflected many times before it leaves, which makes it sparkle.

value: Statements 2 and 3 are essential; 30 degrees C is too hot for wheat
reasoning: Wheat is a cool-season crop: it grows best at about 10 to 15 degrees C during growth and 20 to 25 degrees C at ripening, so an optimum of 30 degrees C (statement 1) is wrong. It needs a frost-free period of roughly 100 days and does best on well-drained loams and clay loams, so 2 and 3 hold. Runner-up: A, if the setter accepted 30 degrees C as a ripening-stage temperature.
Gwadar is a deep-sea port on the Arabian Sea coast of Balochistan, Pakistan, developed with Chinese help under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. Iran's comparable port nearby is Chabahar.

value: At the end of the Cretaceous period (Deccan Traps)
reasoning: The Deccan Traps, the huge basalt flows over north-west peninsular India, were erupted at the close of the Cretaceous period, about 66 million years ago.

Factor out 3^9 (itself a cube): 3^9(1 + 27 + 729 + 3^(n-9)) = 3^9(757 + 3^(n-9)). With n = 14, 3^5 = 243 and 757 + 243 = 1000 = 10^3, so the sum is (3^3 x 10)^3. The other options give 766, 784 and 838, none a cube.

value: The circle has the larger area
reasoning: For perimeter P, the square's area is P^2/16 and the circle's is P^2/(4 pi), about P^2/12.57, which is larger. Of all shapes with a given perimeter, the circle encloses the most area; the ratio is 4/pi, about 1.27, not 2.

The conditions say (x, y) and (u, v) are perpendicular unit vectors, so the matrix with rows (x, y) and (u, v) is orthogonal. Its columns are then also perpendicular unit vectors, giving x^2 + u^2 = 1, y^2 + v^2 = 1 and xy + uv = 0. For example, x = cos t, y = sin t, u = -sin t, v = cos t satisfies all three.
A non-leap year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day. Day 1 and day 365 are 364 days apart, an exact number of weeks, so the last day falls on the same weekday as the first: Sunday.

Facing north, A walks 10 m north, then turns right and walks 10 m east, reaching (10, 10). Turning left each time: 5 m north to (10, 15), 15 m west to (-5, 15), 15 m south to (-5, 0). He ends 5 m west of the starting point.

value: Workers' participation in local self-government is not a Directive Principle
reasoning: Article 41 covers the right to work, education and public assistance, Article 44 a Uniform Civil Code and Article 50 separation of the judiciary from the executive. Article 43A provides for workers' participation in the management of industries, not of local self-government, so D is not provided for.
Under the Mountbatten Plan, the members of the Punjab and Bengal Legislative Assemblies met in two parts (Muslim-majority and other districts) and voted on whether the province should be partitioned.

Weber's ideal type defines bureaucracy by structural features (hierarchy, division of labour, written rules) and behavioural ones (impersonality, rationality, rule-following), so statement 2 is correct. Treating bureaucracy as an instrument of a dominant class is the Marxist view, not Weber's, so statement 1 is wrong. Runner-up: C, if 'dominant class character' were read as Weber's legal-rational domination.

value: DPSPs do not override Fundamental Rights
reasoning: Under Article 37 Directive Principles are not enforceable in court but are fundamental in governance and law-making, and they set out the aims of the State. Fundamental Rights, being enforceable, generally prevail in a conflict (Champakam Dorairajan, Minerva Mills), with only limited protection for laws under Articles 39(b) and (c) through Article 31C. So C is the incorrect statement.

Liberal democracy rests on constitutional government bound by formal legal rules and on guaranteed civil liberties and individual rights. Investing authority with potentially unlimited power is the mark of totalitarian or absolutist rule, the opposite of liberal democracy.

Phreatophytes are deep-rooted plants that draw water from the water table or the soil just above it, an adaptation typical of arid and semi-arid regions (for example mesquite and tamarisk). Runner-up: A, since phreatophytes also grow along streams and moist places, but the textbook association is with arid environments.
Hydra and sea anemone are cnidarians with stinging cells (cnidocytes). Planaria and liver fluke are flatworms, sea urchin and sea cucumber are echinoderms, and Euplectella and Sycon are sponges.

Growth movement of a plant part towards light is positive phototropism, shown by shoots. Roots bending away from light show negative phototropism; photonasty is non-directional and photoperiodism concerns day length and flowering.
Root hairs are tubular outgrowths of root epidermal cells that greatly increase the surface area for absorbing water and minerals.
Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide, SiO2, so it contains silicon.

Sodium hexametaphosphate, sold as Calgon, softens water by forming soluble complexes with calcium and magnesium ions (the Calgon process). Magnesium hydrogencarbonate causes hardness rather than removing it. Runner-up: B, since trisodium phosphate also softens water by precipitating calcium and magnesium phosphates, but Calgon is the standard answer.
Na2X means X carries a charge of 2-. Aluminium forms Al3+, so balancing charges needs 2 Al3+ (+6) for 3 X2- (-6), giving Al2X3.
The simple multiplier is 1 / (1 - MPC) = 1 / (1 - 0.9) = 1 / 0.1 = 10.
In the Keynesian consumption function C = a + bY, the slope b is the marginal propensity to consume, which lies between 0 and 1. Consumption rises with income, so the slope is positive.

value: The price printed on a biscuit packet (MRP)
reasoning: A price ceiling is a legal maximum price, and the maximum retail price printed on a packet is the highest price a seller may charge. Minimum support price and minimum wages are price floors, and airline fares in India are largely market-determined. Runner-up: A, only if the fare caps occasionally imposed on airlines were the intended example.

value: To produce more of one good it must give up some of another
reasoning: A point on the production possibility frontier means resources are fully and efficiently used, so more of one good can be had only by giving up some of the other (opportunity cost). The frontier is downward sloping, and producing more without sacrifice is possible only from inside it.

The paradox of thrift, that higher saving by everyone can lower total income and even total saving, is associated with Keynes's General Theory (1936). Runner-up: D, because Samuelson popularised the term in his textbook, and the idea itself has older roots (Mandeville).
The Indian Forest Act of 1878 divided forests into three categories: reserved, protected and village forests. The first Forest Act of 1865 had no such three-way division.

value: Brahmo Samaj (1828), Paramhans Mandali (1849), Arya Samaj (1875), Ramakrishna Mission (1897)
reasoning: Raja Rammohun Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, the Paramhans Mandali was formed in Bombay in 1849, Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 and Vivekananda the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897. The order is 3, 4, 2, 1.
